title: Scalar restriction identifies the augmented internal and constant quotient towers
statement: For a prime l, a finite extension E/Q_l, any scheme morphism g:X→Y and any cochain complex P of internal continuous integral modules on Y, restriction of scalars along constantToIntegral from [def-sfb-integral-pullback-comparison-data] carries the Roos complex of the pulled quotient tower isomorphically to the Roos complex of the constant pulled quotient tower of Res(P). The composite of the restricted quotient augmentation with this chain isomorphism equals restrictionPullbackComplex followed by constantComparison. This is a chain equality for all P, without K-flatness, constructibility or derived completeness assumptions.

source.place: Comparison with the Stacks Project: scalar restriction commutes with inverse image, finite reduction and R lim

proof.text: The constant-to-continuous coefficient map induces an isomorphism on each positive finite quotient: continuous maps to the finite discrete quotient are locally constant. Thus extension of the constant quotient along the coefficient map is the continuous quotient, compatibly with every quotient transition and unit. Associativity of balanced tensor products yields Res(M tensor_R A_n) ≅ Res(M) tensor_C A_n for every M. Apply these identifications in each degree.

Combine the level comparisons with the normalized restrictionPullback square of [def-sfb-integral-pullback-comparison-data]. Its generator equation identifies the source quotient legs: applying the two composites to a scalar-extension tensor generator gives the same quotient tensor generator. These generators jointly generate the module, so all augmentation and transition squares commute.

Restriction of scalars is exact and preserves products. Compose its canonical product isomorphism with the product of the level comparisons. Check on projections that it intertwines one minus transition shift, then take the induced shifted mapping-cone isomorphism. The restricted augmentation and the constant augmentation have the same first component and zero second component, giving the displayed equality with the prescribed source map restrictionPullbackComplex. No resolving, boundedness or nonempty-scheme assumptions enter this construction.

lean.statement:
theorem constant_roos_unit {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (g : X ⟶ Y)
    (P : CochainComplex (AdicCompletion.Modules l E Y) ℤ) :
    ∃ e : (((restriction l E X).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj
          (WeilConjectures.integralOperationsRoos (pulledTower l E g P))) ≅
        WeilConjectures.integralOperationsRoos
          (constantPulledTower l E g
            (((restriction l E Y).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P)),
      ((restriction l E X).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).map (comparison l E g P) ≫
          e.hom =
        (restrictionPullbackComplex l E g P).hom ≫
          constantComparison l E g
            (((restriction l E Y).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P)
